messages:
maria: customer reported invoice discrepancy after we enabled continuous-batching + kv-prefetch on their dedicated pool. billed tokens ~12% higher than dashboard served tokens. invoice INV-98765, org acme-inc. sample req ids: req_abc123 req_def456

jon: thanks. timeframe? are these concentrated right after the feature flip?

maria: yes flipped at 2024-11-02T14:10Z. spike starts ~14:12Z and lasts ~3h. dashboards show served tokens consistent, invoiced tokens higher. customer hit us via support form.

patrick: adding billing-ops. can you pull metering rows for those req ids and the prefetch events?

billing-ops: pulling now. I see two event types for those requests: prefetch_billed and serve_billed. prefetch_billed timestamps sometimes precede serve_billed by 30-90s. attaching small excerpt.

billing-ops: ```
# metering excerpt (ordered by event_time)
2024-11-02T14:12:05Z prefetch_billed org=acme-inc req=req_abc123 tokens=24
2024-11-02T14:12:38Z serve_billed   org=acme-inc req=req_abc123 tokens=24
2024-11-02T14:12:10Z prefetch_billed org=acme-inc req=req_def456 tokens=18
2024-11-02T14:13:00Z serve_billed   org=acme-inc req=req_def456 tokens=18
```

mike: hmm prefetch_billed should be billed only if prefetch actually fetched from upstream and wasn't deduped when later served from cache. maybe eviction / re-check race?

sre-jen: I pulled runtime logs for the dedicated pool. I see KV cache eviction bursts around 14:12:22Z (OOM grooming) that coincide with continuous-batcher flushes. logs: 

sre-jen: ```
[14:12:22Z] kv_cache: evict prefix pfx_42 (reason=capacity)
[14:12:22Z] cbatch: flush batch_id=327 reqs=48
[14:12:22Z] prefetch: launched pfx_42 for req=req_abc123 -> upstream 10.0.8.4
[14:12:23Z] prefetch: upstream returned tokens=24 status=200
[14:12:38Z] serve: used kv hit for req=req_abc123 tokens=24
```

jon: so the sequence is: eviction happens -> batch triggers prefetch -> prefetch is billed -> later serve reads from cache (after upstream response landed) and we mark as served (not credited). billing pipeline ended up counting both prefetch_billed and serve_billed. Not good.

patrick: is this specific to continuous-batcher? do we see same behavior with on-demand (non-continuous) batching?

sre-jen: limited sampling shows non-continuous mode dedupes prefetch vs serve more reliably because prefetch is attached to the same request lifecycle. continuous-batcher does optimistic prefetching where bookkeeping is decoupled and we kept a ticketed billed event at prefetch completion without a final reconciliation step.

maria: customer expects either billed OR served, not both. they want credits and a root cause.

billing-ops: agreed. created ticket BLG-4532 to reconcile duplicates and issue credits if double-counted. attaching planned fix: add reconciliation pass that joins prefetch_billed events with serve_billed within a configurable window (default 120s) and dedupes billing rows.

billing-ops: proposed patch pseudo: ```
# on invoice pass
for each prefetch_event in window:
  if exists serve_event with same org and prefix and req_id within WINDOW:
    mark prefetch_event as deduped (credit amount)
```

jon: also need runtime mitigation so we don't spam prefetch hits while evictions are in-flight. options: 1) avoid launching prefetch for prefixed keys that were just evicted within Xs, 2) attach correlation id so later serve can claim prefetch cost. which is lowest risk?

sre-jen: short-term: correlation id on prefetch and annotate serve pipeline to check for matching correlation -> drop duplicate billing emit. medium-term: tweak cbatch prefetch gating to back-off after eviction events for 1s.

mike: I'll raise PR for correlation header and update metering emitter to dedupe by correlation_id if present.

mike: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4829 (draft)

patrick: customer credits: billing-ops, estimate amount to credit?

billing-ops: running aggregate over affected window for acme-inc -> approx 11.8% extra tokens billed. calculating exact invoice adjustment, will issue credit and email customer. ticket BLG-4532 updated.

maria: draft response to customer: "We've identified a duplication bug where prefetched prefix requests were sometimes billed and later served causing double-counting. We're issuing a credit for the overage and rolling out a fix. Apologies for the disruption. Will share timeline." ok?

jon: add "we're throttling prefetch for the pool as immediate mitigation" to that.

maria: done. sending now.

support-bot: user message sent to acme-inc at 2024-11-02T16:05:12Z.

mike: merged correlation_id emit change to staging, running e2e against a synthetic workload that reproduces eviction+prefetch race.

sre-jen: can we add an alert if prefetch_billed / serve_billed ratio > 1.05 for any org over 5m window? would catch regressions.

patrick: yes. created monitoring rule MON-2287.

billing-ops: credits issued: INV-98765 credited 12% ($3,180). customer confirmed receipt.

maria: closing thread after we deploy reconciliation and gating. follow-ups tracked in BLG-4532 and PR-4829. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
